chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala' said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who prays the two rak'ahs of the obligatory prayer, does not sit between them until he bows in the third, he said: 'Let him complete his prayer, then give the taslim, and prostrate the two prostrations of forgetfulness while sitting before he speaks.'

key_terms.لْيُسَلِّمْ: let him give the taslim (salutation of peace)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets to sit between the first two rak'ahs of an obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that omitting the intermediate sitting (jalsah bayn as-sajdayn) does not invalidate the prayer but requires rectification through two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdat al-sehv). Notably, the Imam specifies that these prostrations must be performed while seated before speaking, reflecting the Shia emphasis on maintaining ritual composure and avoiding casual conversation immediately after prayer. This ruling underscores the distinction between essential pillars (arkan) and recommended acts (sunan) in Shia jurisprudence.
